name: Italian Constitutional Court, judgment no. 105/2024 – “decreto Priolo” (“Priolo Decree”), Sicily
description: Constitutional review of Article 104-bis, paragraph 1-bis.1, of the implementing provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, introduced by Article 6 of Decree-Law of 5 January 2023, no. 2, the so-called “decreto Priolo” (converted by Law of 3 March 2023, no. 17): extraordinary measures that allowed the continuation of the activity of plants of national strategic interest (in this case, the consortium wastewater treatment plant of Priolo Gargallo, which treats the effluents of the Priolo-Melilli-Augusta petrochemical hub in Sicily, seized on 13 May 2022) despite the existence of seizures ordered by the judicial authority for environmental and health risks. The question was raised by the Judge for Preliminary Investigations (GIP) at the Tribunal of Syracuse.
outcome: Partial unconstitutionality. The Court censured the structural repetition of “extraordinary” measures that sacrifice the protection of health and the environment (Articles 9, 32 and 41 of the Constitution as amended by Constitutional Law no. 1/2022) to the need for production continuity, in the absence of real features of temporariness and of adequate balancing. The first significant application of the new constitutional environmental parameters.
